brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases in a tight cluster: full bases at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1, west half-base at -1,0, north half-base at 0,-1 (about 478 x 500 mm footprint, one storey).
drawer:0#0,-1#cut (classic, south half) on the cut face of the half-base at 0,-1.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Spike at the junction of cells 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0 (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0, mount type).
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that spike; BOM lists Platform, small x1. A solid spike was refused for the platform.
capOpenFaces was refused with MESH_CLASH against the drawer frame, so 18 open faces remain uncapped (info only). lockJoints applied; meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability for desk use (strength, finish)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; material properties are not verified.

finish.summary: Built a compact 4-base desk unit with a south-facing drawer and a mount-type spike carrying a small platform at the three-base corner. check_build reports meshClash clear with no errors. Open faces could not all be capped because a cap clashes with the drawer frame, so they remain uncapped. No props were added since the brief concerns structure. The configurator does not verify material suitability for desk use.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
